summary: A 1930 Columbia Falls kit cabin was replaced in 1959 by the concrete-and-R-6 cab standing today, survived a 1994 fire scare, and is now a Kootenai NF rental.

facts.design: R-6 flat cab on 10-foot concrete base

access.note: Drivable to within a quarter mile; final stretch is steep and rocky, unsuitable for low-clearance vehicles.

visit.trail_note: Sits directly on the Pacific Northwest National Scenic Trail.

facts.agency: US Forest Service, Kootenai National Forest

events.note: 14x14' Columbia Falls 'redi-cut' cab developed on the site.
Original cabin replaced with a 10' concrete base topped by a flat-roofed R-6 cab, the structure standing today.
A forest fire threatened the lookout; it survived.
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register, January 9, 2021.

evidence.supports: 1930 build, Columbia Falls cab, 1959 replacement, tree platform, 1994 fire
evidence.quote: Developed in 1930 with a 14x14' Columbia Falls "redi-cut" cab, this unique structure was replaced in 1959 with the present 10' concrete base topped with an R-6 flat cab. There was also a 35' tree platform 1/2 mile west of the lookout. The cabin is in the rental program, and was threatened by a forest fire in 1994.

evidence.supports: built 1959, used for fire detection 40+ years, rental facilities and access
evidence.quote: The lookout was built in 1959 and used as an observation point for fighting forest fires for over 40 years.
the last quarter mile of the access road is steep and rocky and not suited for low clearance vehicles

evidence.supports: Pacific Northwest National Scenic Trail location
evidence.quote: Webb Mountain Lookout is on the Pacific Northwest National Scenic Trail, you may be visited by through hikers.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR/firelookout.com date the site to 1930 (first cabin); recreation.gov dates the current structure to 1959 (its replacement). Both are correct for what they describe.

notes_for_editor: Brief's events/facts matched sources closely; no corrections needed. firelookout.com page was consistent with NHLR text (likely same underlying description) so not separately cited. Fact-check 2026-10-04: removed an unsupported claim that fire detection 'shifted to aircraft' after Webb's 40+ years of use; neither cited source says this.
